items.summary: A massive manhunt is underway across Tamil Nadu after 17 remand prisoners escaped from the Theni sub-jail on Monday night. The inmates staged an illness before assaulting three prison personnel, and four have been apprehended while 13 remain at large. Tamil Nadu Police deployed drones and formed 17 special teams to track them down; the state government suspended nine jail staff over lapses amid political controversy.
items.title: Seventeen Prisoners Escape Theni Sub-Jail After Faking Illness

items.summary: Cyclone Arnab has intensified into a very severe cyclonic storm over the Bay of Bengal and is heading toward India's east coast. The India Meteorological Department issued a red alert across Andhra Pradesh and southern Odisha, forecasting heavy to extremely heavy rainfall with maximum sustained winds reaching 115 to 125 kilometres per hour, gusting up to 140 kilometres per hour. Landfall is expected along the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam. National Disaster Response Force teams have been deployed across multiple states; the Indian Navy and Coast Guard remain on standby. Coastal administrations initiated evacuations from low-lying areas, set up relief shelters, declared holidays for schools and colleges, and directed fishermen to avoid the sea as authorities aim for zero casualties.
items.title: Cyclone Arnab Intensifies; Red Alert, Evacuations Under Way

items.summary: Several Chinese brands dropped French footballer Kylian Mbappé as online backlash grew over alleged comments referring to the late leader Mao Zedong, whose death in 1976 ended an era that began China's opening to the global economy. In unverified clips from The Bridge talk show, Mbappé joked about a meme he thought showed 'a Chinese dictator,' though he never named Mao and the original video is gone. Foreign ministry spokesperson Lin Jian said hurt feelings would meet opposition across society; forum Dongqiudi called the remarks inappropriate. Mengniu and drinks firm Dongpeng both cited zero-tolerance policies toward offending national sentiment, while CCTV reportedly suspended La Liga matches.
items.title: Chinese brands drop Mbappé over Mao joke backlash

items.summary: Israeli opposition leaders urged voters on Tuesday, 27 October 2026, to turn out in large numbers during parliamentary elections scheduled from 7 am (0500GMT) until 10 pm (2000GMT), aiming to end Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s rule. Avigdor Lieberman of Yisrael Beiteinu called for voting to conclude the Netanyahu era and Haredi influence, while Gadi Eisenkot of Yashar stressed his party must become largest. Gilad Kariv warned Netanyahu allies would spread misinformation and framed turnout as essential.
items.title: Israeli Opposition Leaders Urge High Voter Turnout in Parliamentary Elections

items.summary: Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge retorted ‘Modi ka baap bhi…’ at a Patna rally, prompting analysis that the remark shifted focus from Opposition questions on electoral roll irregularities. The piece argues Congress had built momentum around alleged Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process flaws, with Election Commissioners Sandhu and Joshi objecting 14 times over 10 months to Kumar’s decisions. Kharge’s comment revived BJP’s ‘chaiwala’ narrative from Mani Shankar Aiyar’s 2014 remark. The author traces coarsening political discourse since the 1990s, noting BJP re-Sanskritised official language especially since 2014. The Federal states its views are those of the author and need not reflect institutional positions.
items.title: Kharge’s slip of tongue gives BJP fresh ammunition

items.summary: Meyer, South Africa's ambassador to Washington and former chief negotiator in the talks that ended apartheid, said on Monday he remained positive despite strained relations with the United States. Speaking at a Cape Town memoir launch, Meyer called for direct dialogue between both governments as the first step toward negotiations. He acknowledged current tension but expressed hope it could be resolved.
items.title: South Africa's US Ambassador Calls for Repairing Strained Ties

items.summary: An investigation by Spotlight on Corruption found that officials developing the UK’s flagship AI and datacentre “growth zones” policy met 137 businesses but only two community groups and no environmental organisations between July 2024 and September 2026. The nonprofit filed 40 freedom of information requests across 18 government agencies over about 12 months, arguing the process was shaped by a “considerable revolving door” as officials moved to AI firms such as OpenAI and Anthropic. A government spokesperson said it works with industry, local authorities, environmental groups and communities while prioritising clean power and responsible water use. The Guardian has separately questioned the policy’s financial figures and job projections.
items.title: UK AI datacentre policy excluded environmental groups, investigation finds

items.summary: The Italian army says a significant cache of unexploded first world war bombs emerged this summer from rapidly retreating glaciers in the Dolomites. The Julia Alpine brigade removed and defused 250 explosives, including 18 Italian 75mm artillery shells and 37 French-made Thevetot mortar shells, after hikers reported sightings near Canal San Bovo. Experts attribute the discoveries to global heating, warning that re-emerging devices are dangerous and access is becoming unsafe as glaciers retreat.
items.title: Retreating Dolomites Glaciers Surface WWI Bomb Cache

items.summary: The Chamber of Trade and Industry has written again to Rahul Gandhi, urging the postponement of the INDIA bloc's proposed November 1 rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan. The traders warn that traffic restrictions during peak Diwali shopping could cause business losses worth Rs 10,000 crore. They estimate around 10 lakh protesters will attend and cite an earlier Jantar Mantar protest linked to losses of Rs 3,000 crore as precedent. Rahul Gandhi rejected the appeal on October 26, linking protests to demands for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's removal. The CTI offered alternatives including Burari Grounds or Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium. No change has been confirmed.
items.title: Delhi Traders Urge INDIA Bloc to Postpone November Rally Over Diwali Losses

items.summary: UK retailers reported sharp increases in sales of essential goods following Defence Secretary Wes Streeting's call for people to stock up against emergencies. Iceland cited a 40% rise in tinned product sales over the weekend, while Maplin saw jumps of 92% in radios, 284% in torches and 106% in power banks since last week's announcement. Josh Pringle reported tenfold growth at Sgt Prepper's store.
items.title: Retailers Report Sales Surge After Government Stockpile Appeal

items.summary: Crude oil prices fell after reports of renewed Middle East peace talks, with Saudi, Turkish, and Pakistani officials visiting Tehran. Brent crude traded at $114.85 per barrel and WTI at $100.87, down from over $117 and over $103 respectively on profit-taking. Continued Houthi attacks and Iranian strikes support prices, while a CNN report suggests U.S. forces could strike Iran within 96 hours of an order.
items.title: Oil Prices Fall on Peace Hopes Despite Iran Strike Threats

items.summary: The Crossword Book Awards announced its 2026 Popular Choice shortlists across five categories, drawn from sales at Crossword Bookstores. Voting runs October 26 to November 23, with winners revealed in December 2026.
items.title: Crossword Book Awards Names Its 2026 Popular Choice Shortlists

items.summary: As Israel heads to its first election since the October 7, 2023 attack, opinion polls show Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party in a close race with former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, neither assured of the parliamentary majority needed to form a government. The contest is framed as a referendum on Netanyahu's leadership amid demands for accountability over an assault that killed around 1,200 people and led to the abduction of 251 people to Gaza. Issues include security, judicial overhaul, military service exemptions for Haredi men, ethnic tensions after a racist remark against Eisenkot, Arab voter turnout expected to rise from about 53 per cent in 2022 to around 63 per cent, and growing scepticism that Israel and an independent Palestinian state could coexist peacefully. The outcome will depend on which camp can assemble at least 61 lawmakers.
items.title: Israel Election Campaign Tests Netanyahu Amid War, Conscription and Ethnic Tensions

items.summary: The Indian Institute of Science Education and Research Pune removed activist Umar Khalid’s book, Fractured Communities: Adivasi Histories and the Politics of Power, from its library to “avoid any misunderstanding or unrest,” The Indian Express quoted the administration as saying. Board chairperson Madabhushi Madan Gopal said he was shocked it had been added last night and that action is initiated on those responsible.
items.title: IISER Pune Pulls Umar Khalid Book From Library

items.summary: Sona BLW Precision Forgings reported a 35% year-on-year rise in consolidated revenue to Rs 1,535.8 crore for Q2FY27, with net profit up 29% to Rs 223.4 crore and EBITDA at Rs 356 crore. Battery electric vehicle revenue grew 129%, reaching 51% of automotive sales. Managing Director Vivek Vikram Singh cited strong BEV growth and order wins behind the gains.
items.title: Sona BLW Reports Strong Q2 Profit and Revenue Growth

items.summary: A localized ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia took effect at 3 a.m. Tuesday ahead of a humanitarian mission into the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky, brokered by first lady Melania Trump after talks with civilian negotiators from both sides. Up to 2,000 people remain stranded there amid dwindling food and medicine. Missile attacks continued elsewhere: Kyiv saw one killed and 10 injured Monday.
items.title: Ceasefire Brokered by Melania Trump Begins in Southern Ukraine

items.summary: Sudan's Rapid Support Forces launched a coordinated drone attack Monday against five power stations, hitting two each in Al-Jazira and Gedaref states plus one in White Nile state. A government official told AFP the strikes caused mass outages across these army-controlled regions. Residents report electricity has been down since 2 am, straining those relying on refrigerated medication.
items.title: RSF Drone Strikes Trigger Widespread Blackouts in Eastern Sudan

items.summary: A limited ceasefire has begun in Oleshky, a Russian-occupied city near Kherson, about a week after US First Lady Melania Trump announced it. Ukrainian officials and Russia's defence ministry say the truce is being respected to allow aid deliveries and civilian evacuation planned for Friday. Residents remain desperate; Ukraine estimates around 6,000 people still live there.
items.title: Truce Begins in Wartorn Ukraine City After It Was Announced by Melania Trump

items.summary: Dan Guthrie, director general of the Alliance for Intellectual Property in the UK, argues that Australia's rush to attract US big tech investment through extreme copyright reforms threatens a decades-old creative ecosystem. He says the proposed opt-out model would give AI companies unrestricted access to Australian and international content at no cost to creators, weakening their rights and market value. Guthrie urges the Albanese government to slow down and choose an Australian way rather than one dictated by US tech.
items.title: UK creative advocate warns Australia risks damaging its creative sector over AI copyright reforms

items.summary: On October 25, Serbia's student-led Student List movement won a historic victory in parliamentary elections, defeating outgoing President Aleksandar Vucic's Serbian Progressive Party (SNS), which had dominated politics for 14 years. The Student List secured 52.45 percent of the vote and 138 seats; the SNS list received 39.2 percent and 103 seats. Supporters said their controllers reported incidents such as parallel lists and carousel voting, asserting that tracking fraud impacted results. Turnout reached 69 percent with more than 4.4 million citizens voting. CRTA noted ballot photos at up to 50 percent of monitored stations. The movement vows to reform institutions and fight corruption; the next presidential election is set for December 2026.
items.title: Serbian Students Defeat Long-Ruling Party Amid Election-Fraud Monitoring

items.summary: Governments voted 83 to 12 at the UN’s main organized-crime forum in Vienna to begin negotiating a global protocol against environmental crimes, including timber, minerals, wildlife and waste. Brazil led the effort with partners across Latin America and Africa despite opposition from the United States, Argentina, Saudi Arabia and Iran. Authors Laura Waisbich, Melina Risso and Robert Muggah argue it would close legal gaps letting illicit goods enter legitimate markets. The protocol will bind only ratifying states, and a draft is unlikely soon.
items.title: UN forum votes to negotiate first global environmental crime protocol

items.summary: Microsoft said on Monday it is offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees, or more than a quarter of its global workforce, as the company looks to contain costs and help fund AI investments. Eligible staff across Windows experiences, Copilot, finance, human resources, Xbox and Windows + Devices would qualify; marketing, commercial business and security are excluded. The program is time-limited and voluntary, built on insights from a previous retirement program. Chief People Officer Amy Coleman said it gives employees considering leaving another choice to transition with support. Microsoft had 223,000 full-time employees globally as of June 30, 2026, per its annual filing.
items.title: Microsoft Offers Buyouts to Around 60,000 Employees

items.summary: Nvidia backed Indian startup Simplismart in a $14 million all-primary Series B round led by Dallas Venture Capital, alongside Accel, Shastra VC and Micromax. The deal values the four-year-old Bengaluru-based company at about $100 million including the new funding. Simplismart’s software automates how AI models run on existing infrastructure to cut GPU costs; it says client InVideo reduced GPU serving costs by 56%. Co-founder Amritanshu Jain told TechCrunch that revenue has grown 14-fold over six months, though he did not disclose the exact figure. The investment appears paradoxical as Nvidia backs software enabling fewer GPUs, but Jain argued efficiency could boost demand for its chips.
items.title: Nvidia Backs Simplismart in $14 Million Series B

items.summary: Days after launching its folding iPhone Duo, Apple acknowledged on Monday that some units show display problems and said it will replace them. Customers reported cracks and lines in the inner display along the central hinge via social media posts over the weekend. In a statement, Apple said affected units tend to fail quickly and directed users to contact AppleCare for a replacement. The company did not comment on what might cause the issue or on iFixit's findings that the fault may stem from a support bar failing to clear during folding.
items.title: Apple Offers Replacements for iPhone Duo Display Faults

items.summary: Bank of America, Blackstone, Citi and Morgan Stanley announced a $63 billion transaction to fund AI computing capacity for Anthropic using Broadcom technology. The deal uses a special purpose vehicle that will buy Broadcom's XPU accelerators and networking products then lease them to Anthropic, with deliveries expected in 2027. Bank of America, Citi and Morgan Stanley hold the first lien tranche; Blackstone holds the second. Broadcom shares rose on Monday. Hock Tan said AI compute demand continues growing at an extraordinary pace.
items.title: Broadcom Syndicate Arranges $63 Billion for Anthropic AI Chips

items.summary: Benchmark indices ended virtually unchanged on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, though the market was sharply divided. Infosys dragged IT stocks down over 1.4 per cent after cutting its FY27 revenue outlook, while smallcap stocks surged 2.69 per cent. Analyst Ajit Mishra of Religare Broking said volatility reflected continued uncertainty following a recent correction. The government cleared a ₹2.12 lakh crore defence package with 82 per cent for domestic manufacturers as another catalyst.
items.title: Indian Markets Flat as Infosys Weakness Weighs on IT Stocks

items.summary: Microsoft clarified that its voluntary exit offer does not replace layoffs, which remain part of the company's approach depending on business conditions. The programme is open to eligible employees at internal level 70 and below in participating teams, with no age or tenure requirements. GeekWire reported roughly 30% accepted an earlier retirement programme in 2026. Eligible staff have until the first week of December 2026 to decide; declining does not guarantee continued employment or a layoff.
items.title: Microsoft Clarifies Voluntary Exit Offer Is Not a Layoff Substitute

items.summary: A man lost a white earbud among pale stones in a parking lot on Friday evening and searched for about ten minutes without success. He then uploaded photos to ChatGPT, which reportedly identified the spot within under a minute; he shared his surprise experience on Reddit.
items.title: Man Finds Lost Earbud With ChatGPT After 10-Minute Search Fails

items.summary: Global stock markets rose on Tuesday after Anthropic's long-awaited IPO prospectus renewed optimism in the AI sector. The firm reported revenue growing fourteenfold in the first half of 2026 versus 2025 and disclosed a $112 billion cash pile, though its $80 billion loss over the same period did little to frighten investors as Nasdaq rose more than 1%. While some hope Big Tech earnings this week will stabilize markets wary of excessive AI spending, others warn of risks reminiscent of China's bursting AI bubble.
items.title: Anthropic IPO Prospectus Boosts Investor Confidence Amid AI Market Uncertainty

items.summary: Days after launching its first folding phone, Apple acknowledged on Monday that some early iPhone Duo units show cracks and lines in the inner display along the central hinge. The reports came from social media posts over the weekend. Affected users are told to contact AppleCare for a replacement. Apple did not comment on what might cause the issue.
items.title: Apple Offers Replacements for Faulty iPhone Duo Displays

items.summary: Disha Daga, a 26-year-old Pune artist who trained as a dancer rather than an artist, has painted mandala murals at the Reserve Bank of India’s Pune office and worked with corporate clients in Malaysia, Thailand, the United States and Jamnagar. Her practice began around 2016 from college notebooks after she discovered mandalas online. She transitioned to full-time art during the pandemic, with her first commercial project in August 2021. According to The Indian Express, workshops have reached more than 25,000 students; Artoreal reports over 120 large-scale artworks and an Instagram following of more than 42,000. Daga notes income depends on commissions and outreach, and she hopes her path encourages young people toward non-conventional careers.
items.title: Pune Artist Disha Daga Paints for RBI and Teaches Thousands

items.summary: Mohammed Shaka of Dubai visited an Apple store with his collection of 53 old iPhones to buy two new foldable iPhone Duo units. His collection spans from the first iPhone launched in 2007 to the iPhone 18 Pro Max, gathered over about 20 years.
items.title: Dubai Man Carries 53 Old iPhones While Buying Two New Foldables

items.summary: AI expert Prof Soumitra Dutta argues India need not compete with global firms on capital and computing power. He explains that the more relevant contest is adopting open-source models at scale across agriculture, health, education and public services. While a local-language advantage exists, he warns it may be temporary unless backed by trusted relationships and rich domain data. The IndiaAI Mission has onboarded about 38,000 GPUs, but chips and cloud software largely come from abroad, so full self-reliance is not realistic soon.
items.title: India should prioritize AI adoption over building its own frontier models, says expert Dutta.

items.summary: Meta-owned Instagram is testing a new feature called Features, letting selected creators in Brazil and the United States upload horizontal videos up to 90 minutes long. The move shifts away from its short-form Reels focus toward longer content like podcasts, interviews and comedy programmes, aiming to compete more directly with YouTube. Reports by Moneycontrol and TechCrunch say Instagram is also testing ways to link short clips to full-length versions so viewers stay within the app. Meta has not announced a long-term advertising revenue-sharing model for Features.
items.title: Instagram Tests 90-Minute Videos to Rival YouTube and Keep Creators

items.summary: Anthropic's S-1 filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission shows Claude produced more than 90% of contributions to its codebase in September, according to the company. The document sets up a Nasdaq listing under ticker ANT, possibly as early as next month. Engineers now mostly direct and review AI output rather than writing code line by line.
items.title: Anthropic's IPO Filing Reveals AI-Driven Shift in Software Engineering Work

items.summary: Leaks suggest Apple's upcoming budget iPhone 18e, expected to launch in 2027, will keep a 60Hz display while gaining a faster chip and sharper front camera. The details come from unnamed tipsters on Weibo and reports cited by TechPulse, including a possible India price under Rs 1 lakh. Apple has not confirmed any of the specifications.
items.title: Leaked iPhone 18e Specs Point To Budget Model With 60Hz Screen

items.summary: Apple backported security patches for a zero-day bug in CoreGraphics, exploited in extremely sophisticated targeted attacks on iOS devices. The out-of-bounds write weakness (CVE-2026-86950) was discovered by Meta Product Security and affects older iPhones and iPads. Apple warned the issue may have been used against specific individuals before iOS 27, advising users to install patches immediately.
items.title: Apple Backports CoreGraphics Zero-Day Patches to Older Devices

items.summary: Meta and Nvidia announced on Tuesday a partnership deepening their collaboration on the Muse AI assistant, with Nvidia investing $3 billion in Meta's equity offering. The models run on Nvidia infrastructure and will work more closely to improve performance and reduce costs. Separately, Meta raised its equity offering to $97.5 billion, its largest ever, as it accelerates investment in AI infrastructure.
items.title: Nvidia and Meta Expand AI Partnership With $3 Billion Deal

items.summary: An S-1 filing reported that Anthropic's seven co-founders pledged to donate about $80 billion, roughly 80% of their stakes. The company plans a Nasdaq listing under ticker ANT, with reports valuing it between $1.5 trillion and $2 trillion. Despite giving away most wealth, founders would retain 50.1% voting power via one Class F share issued to an LLC they control. Each founder's stake could reach about $27 billion at a $2 trillion valuation. Fortune reported the figures.
items.title: Anthropic Founders Plan Charity Pledge Amid IPO

items.summary: Google Cloud, with the Informatics Industry Association of Türkiye, launched a national cloud and AI upskilling academy to certify more than 1,000 professionals within a year. Announced at Google Cloud Day Türkiye in Istanbul on Tuesday, the program aligns with the company's planned $2 billion local cloud region investment and supports Turkey's 2026-2030 AI action plan. Country manager Onder Guler emphasized that advanced technology delivers value only when local talent can drive it.
items.title: Google Cloud and Turkish Association Launch AI Upskilling Program

items.summary: In its Monday IPO filing, Anthropic detailed a governance structure designed to outlast its founders. The lab gave co-founders 50.1% voting power over certain matters while an independent trust controls most board seats and Class T stock will let it elect a majority of directors. As a public benefit corporation with expected $1.5 trillion valuation, Anthropic expects the AI could one day cure cancer or kill up to 8 billion people. The company declined to comment.
items.title: Anthropic's Governance Plan for Long After Its Founders Depart

items.summary: Former RBI Governor Raghuram Rajan cautioned against using India's foreign exchange reserves to defend a specific rupee rate, urging policymakers toward longer-term thinking. The rupee fell about 6% in 2026 and hit a record low of 96.96 against the dollar in May. Rajan said 'don't panic,' noting depreciation could aid exports while oil prices pose risks.
items.title: Rajan Warns RBI Against Spending Reserves To Defend Rupee

items.summary: A US federal judge on Monday (Oct 27) granted Alibaba Group Holding's request for a preliminary injunction, barring the government from denying Pentagon contracts to firms that lobby for companies designated as aiding China's military. The ruling lets Alibaba keep shared lobbyists and supports its legal challenge against the designation, though it does not remove Alibaba from the list or lift sanctions.
items.title: Alibaba Wins Injunction Against Pentagon Lobbying Ban

items.summary: Robert Reich argues that billionaire wealth should be taxed and big money removed from politics, using Elon Musk as the central example of why billionaires should not control media or hold government contracts. Reich cites a Wall Street Journal report that Musk ordered a slowdown of military-grade Starlink used by Ukraine, which he attributed to violations of service terms. He rejects claims that Musk is an innovator and calls both Musk and Trump conmen who corrupt governments for personal gain. Reich notes Musk has spent roughly $445m in the 2026 midterm cycle and at least $168m on Texas Super Pacs, making him the largest single known donor. He urges readers to defund Musk, stop buying Teslas, avoid X and Starlink, and support politicians who would end his government contracts.
items.title: Robert Reich Calls for Defunding Elon Musk

items.summary: Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees in India, Canada, the United States and the United Kingdom as it increases its artificial intelligence investment. AFP reported that the offer covers roughly 27% of Microsoft's global workforce, with eligibility limited to staff at the vice-president level and below while excluding some data centre, sales and marketing roles.
items.title: Microsoft Extends Voluntary Exit Offers as It Doubles Down on AI Investment

items.summary: In Taphou Kuki, near Imphal, a village chief sees his Naga neighbours across the divide and compares their hostility to India's 1999 war with Pakistan. The article frames this as part of renewed Naga-Kuki fighting that has spread through Manipur since May 2023, killing more than 300 people and displacing around 60,000 since then. A hostage crisis in June marked an escalation; one side says it abducted villagers after being attacked first, while the other denies holding captives. Both sides describe their own weapons as defence and accuse each other of planned aggression over land. The government has not accepted a proposed union territory for Kuki areas, citing territorial integrity.
items.title: Neighbours split by ethnic violence in Manipur

items.summary: As Anthropic prepares for its stock market debut, the company's 335-page IPO paperwork devotes 93 pages to risk factors, far more than rival SpaceX's 38 of over 250 pages. The disclosures cover autonomous systems that could act without oversight, misuse by malicious actors for cyberattacks or weapons development, and competition for expensive computing power amid community opposition to data centres. Founders wrote in the filing: 'To build AI is to harness cognition itself.' CEO Dario Amodei warned within six to 12 months AI could lead a swarm of agents taking over the internet. Analyst Brian Mulberry of Zacks Investment noted IPO deals must clearly outline risks, underscoring the transparency required for public companies.
items.title: Anthropic's IPO Filing Highlights AI Safety and Operational Risks

items.summary: Fatih Birol, head of the International Energy Agency, warned that global clean energy supply chains are dangerously concentrated, declining to name any countries involved. China is by far the most dominant player in transition technology capacity and investment, making the most wind and solar equipment while also being the world’s largest battery maker and electric car seller. Reuters reported Birol cited a speech at Singapore International Energy Week; climate outlet Ember showed Southeast Asia was the main destination for Chinese tech since January 2025, buying $20 billion worth of such products.
items.title: IEA Chief Warns of Concentrated Clean Energy Supply Chains

items.summary: OCBC was ranked third-strongest bank globally and strongest in Singapore and the Asia-Pacific in The Asian Banker's TAB Global 1000 World's Strongest Banks 2026 ranking, released Oct 27. It is the first Singapore bank to finish among the top three since the ranking debuted in 2023; JPMorgan Chase and Saudi National Bank ranked above it. OCBC also led the Straits Times Index with its share price up 46.6 per cent so far this year, following a record second-quarter net profit of $2.22 billion, up 22 per cent from the prior year.
items.title: OCBC Named Asia-Pacific's Strongest Bank in Global Ranking

items.summary: Mainboard-listed ST Engineering reported on Oct 27 that it secured $5.6 billion worth of new contracts, which it described as a strong third quarter for the global technology, defence and engineering group. Nearly half came from its urban solutions and satcom segment at some $2.4 billion; another $1.8 billion went to its defence and public security business segment, with the remaining $1.4 billion won by its commercial aerospace unit. This brought total contract wins for the nine months of 2026 to $13.2 billion.
items.title: ST Engineering Bags $5.6 Billion in Q3 Contracts

items.summary: IBM researchers connected two IBM Quantum Nighthawk R1 processors using four meter-scale l-couplers, each with an 80-centimeter cable. The work achieved quantum state transfer fidelities of up to 99.3%, averaging 99% over the links, and a two-qubit gate fidelity of 94.75% for distant CZ gates built across all four connections. IBM describes this as the first time superconducting processors have been linked with multiple meter-scale channels at that average fidelity, calling it a milestone toward fault-tolerant scaling. The l-couplers include cables, simplified qubits, tunable couplers and controllers installed after mounting in dilution refrigerators. Researchers note all reported metrics still need improvement as they work toward IBM Quantum Starling.
items.title: IBM Demonstrates Modular Quantum Processor Links

items.summary: In Kananga, Democratic Republic of Congo, a randomised controlled trial compared progressive and proportional property tax schedules calibrated to the same average liability. Progressive neighbourhoods raised 56% more revenue per property than proportional ones (source s0), and 63% more than prior flat fees (s26). Gains came from higher compliance at every point of the distribution, not fairness perceptions: disclosing rates did not increase payment (s41–s48). In 2025, targeted enforcement on valuable properties raised compliance by 19 percentage points and flipped effective tax rates upward-sloping (s61,s62). The authors conclude schedule shape matters for revenue but statutory progressivity alone does not guarantee a progressive burden without enforcement.
items.title: Progressive Property Tax Raised Revenue in DRC City Experiment

items.summary: OpenAI announced that its models produced three verified results, including a proof of the local smoothing conjecture across all dimensions, a disproof of the Exponential Time Hypothesis, and existence proofs for quantum field theories. The company called them raw research data awaiting external review by expert groups it funded. Outside mathematicians and physicists will shepherd verification; OpenAI acknowledged that unverified AI proofs may contain errors.
items.title: OpenAI Announces AI-Verified Proofs in Math and Physics

items.summary: Ong Eng Hong wrote to Parliament responding to a letter on HDB corridor clutter. He said flats along common corridors are usually the same size and that his own floor is mostly clean except for two or three units where bicycles, flower pots and laundry are stored. He argued enforcement matters as much as rules, saying it would make a mockery of them if not enforced, and asked why some residents can keep items inside while others clutter shared space.
items.title: Corridor clutter should be firmly addressed, says resident

items.summary: On Oct 27, 2026, Lila Bailey and Tess Vartanian argue that the federal Stealth Bot Prohibition Act and New York’s Stealth Crawler Prohibition Act would harm legitimate automated data collection without addressing abusive crawling. They note more than 300 media representatives advocated for the bill on Capitol Hill last month. The authors contend these bills threaten tools used in journalism, research, archiving, and security, citing a 2022 Wall Street Journal investigation that analyzed over 31,000 financial disclosures from 12,000 senior government employees via web scraping. They warn the federal bill could impose penalties of up to $53,000 for stealth bots without defining harm, while New York’s allows subpoenas without showing injury. The authors call instead for technical standards and conduct-based liability.
items.title: Two Authors Argue Stealth Bot Bills Harm Legitimate Crawling

items.summary: The UK-US Tech Prosperity Deal has tentatively returned to negotiations, though the revival is partial and agreement over the Digital Services Tax and online safety rules remains stalled. The deal originally rested on an informal memorandum covering nuclear energy, quantum technologies, joint AI research and data centre exports; linked investment pledges of £31 billion have since been abandoned amid public opposition. Renewed talks raise questions about whether the Burnham government will trade away digital regulatory powers to appease Trump and avoid tariffs, even as uncertainty persists over what benefit Britain stands to gain from closer ties with Washington.
items.title: UK-US Tech Deal Revival Raises Questions Over Britain's AI Goals

items.summary: At the Hindu and SRMIST's Semiconductor Summit 2026, stakeholders said India's semiconductor success depends on resilient supply chains spanning fabrication to high-tech equipment. Executives noted OSAT investments could build a wider ecosystem. Sharath Kaul of INEMI called advanced packaging a golden opportunity for India to accelerate. Sandeep Garg of Indichip Semiconductors flagged that students are not industry-ready, urging curriculum changes.
items.title: India Aims for Resilient Semiconductor Supply Chains at Summit

items.summary: The Supreme Court said it would examine the Election Commission of India's decision-making process amid allegations that key decisions, including Special Intensive Revision (SIR) roll changes and Form 6 amendments in Bihar, were taken unilaterally. Chief Justice Surya Kant told petitioners to preserve file notings while granting them 10 days to reply to the ECI's affidavit, which denied the claims and said its filing was unanimous. The bench adjourned until November 17.
items.title: Supreme Court Orders Petitioners' Reply on ECI's Unanimity Claims

items.summary: Congress leader Sonia Gandhi said on Tuesday that a "tamasha" would follow the November release of her memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love. Writing in a video posted to X, she called much prior writing about her exaggerated or invented and said the book lets her record facts as they were. She added some readers may change their views while others grow more negative, calling it inevitable for public figures. The Indian edition is published by HarperCollins India; an earlier dispute with Penguin Random House over editorial changes was resolved when HarperCollins stepped in.
items.title: Sonia Gandhi Warns of 'Tamasha' as Memoir Looms

items.summary: China extended deep condolences for the death of former Japanese Prime Minister Yasuo Fukuda, described by Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun on Monday. He said Fukuda long championed China-Japan friendship and upheld a correct view of history. The statement framed him as an old friend committed to bilateral ties.
items.title: China Offers Condolences as Japan's Fukuda Dies

items.summary: At a regular news briefing, Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said China abides by agreements with India and conducts routine border patrols to safeguard its sovereignty. The remarks came in response to Indian allegations that Chinese forces disturbed the peace along the border. Guo expressed hope that both sides would work together through diplomatic and military channels to maintain tranquility.
items.title: China Calls on India for Joint Efforts Along Shared Border

items.summary: The Union Tribal Affairs Ministry told the Calcutta High Court that Nicobarese leaders seeking to join a petition on Great Nicobar forest rights are “neither necessary nor proper parties,” arguing they were “sleeping over” their rights. Petitioners allege the 2022 settlement relied on consent from non-tribal settlers, though the Ministry’s own annual report shows zero claims settled in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands as of March 2025. Souparna Lahiri of the Global Forest Coalition said it was surprising for the ministry to “go so starkly against its own beneficiaries.” The Calcutta High Court has scheduled hearings on November 25 and 26.
items.title: Tribal Ministry Rejects Nicobarese Standing in Forest Rights Case

items.summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won a fourth term, securing 51.8% of the vote against right-wing challenger Flavio Bolsonaro after an intensive runoff campaign combining youth mobilisation, a revamped social media strategy and opposition to the Bolsonaro family. The 80-year-old incumbent had called his first-round effort "the most disorganized" in decades. Political scientist Eduardo Grin said young-voter mobilisation was fundamental; publicist Taiza Mendonca described heavy online work. The Lula's Army WhatsApp channel grew from 60,000 followers to nearly 11 million in about three weeks. Campaign measures included a two-days-rest reform and rescheduled welfare payments. While timing may have kept issues prominent, the item notes available information does not establish each measure's independent electoral impact.
items.title: Four factors behind Lula's fourth-term election win

items.summary: Congress leader Sonia Gandhi said she was totally against her husband Rajiv Gandhi becoming Prime Minister, revealing the anecdote while promoting her memoir Belonging: A Journey of Love. Posted on October 22 for its Instagram and X debut, the book is set to be published November 10 and may trigger a tamasha as it presents her account of events, including declining the post after the Congress-led alliance won the 2004 election.
items.title: Sonia Gandhi Says She Opposed Rajiv Becoming PM Amid Memoir Hype

items.summary: Luke Anstee, a 23-year-old IT worker in his final university year, hopes the government's Your First Home scheme could let him buy a first home with a deposit as low as 2.5%. Further details are expected in Wednesday's Budget. He said he had rarely stayed anywhere for more than three years and would be hesitant to take on extra borrowing, warning it felt like a gamble if interest rates rose.
items.title: First-time buyer weighs proposed housing loan scheme amid cost pressures

items.summary: Two leading Chinese brands, Dongpeng and Mengniu, suspended their sponsorship agreements with Kylian Mbappé after a video circulated in which he appears to joke about Mao Zedong. Both companies ended cooperation immediately, citing zero tolerance for behaviour that offends national feelings. The split marks a sharp reversal from his previously strong popularity among Chinese fans.
items.title: Chinese Sponsors Drop Mbappé Over Mao Zedong Joke

items.summary: California, which has the most installed solar capacity in the country, still lacks a functioning community solar program despite years of effort. The California Legislature mandated one in 2022 through AB 2316, requiring large utilities to let ratepayers join offsite renewable generation. Talks with the CPUC and investor-owned utilities stalled after outgoing Gov. Gavin Newsom vetoed AB 1813 in September, arguing it would raise consumer bills without reliable grid capacity. Advocates say the veto ignores cost assumptions and pushes developers toward other states; Aaron Halimi of Renewable Properties said resources will shift to those markets. Derek Chernow of CLASS pledged continued pressure ahead of a December legislative session with a new governor until September 2027.
items.title: California Still Lacks a Working Community Solar Program After Veto

items.summary: An excerpt from Shastri Akella's collection A Queer Shade of Saffron centers on Boy, who works at Lajawab Highway Dhaba near Delhi. He meets Madhu, a boy displaced by flooding in Garhwal, whom he invites to work beside him. Their conversation turns to cruelty when they witness a mini truck carrying dozens of dogs destined for a pit; the driver slows so Madhu can see them suffer. Paramjit Singh explains that Ajay, his cousin and an old bully, rounds up stray animals citywide after charging neighborhoods fees. Boy hopes karma will punish him.
items.title: Queer short fiction follows a dhaba worker and his new friend in India

items.summary: Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi, former Tamil Nadu School Education Minister and DMK leader, was arrested in Chennai on October 26, 2026, becoming the first former minister detained after the TVK government took office in May 2026. The Madras High Court dismissed his anticipatory bail petition that same day; Justice V. Lakshminarayanan said granting bail would paralyse the investigation into alleged Rs.400 crore collected from 177 private schools, possibly on the pretext of securing government approvals. Mahesh was remanded until November 6 and charged under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita sections for criminal breach of trust and cheating. DMK president M.K. Stalin condemned the arrest as a political move to conceal law-and-order problems, while BJP leader K. Annamalai welcomed it. A parallel Enforcement Directorate probe began October 1. The article also notes prosecution sanction was granted by the State government on September 7 rather than the Governor, raising legal questions about ministerial prosecutions.
items.title: Former Tamil Nadu Education Minister Arrested on Corruption Charges

items.summary: Heat pump installers in England warn that planned subsidy cuts announced for Wednesday’s budget could damage their businesses, which rely heavily on government support. Bill Tuck of Sustain Homes said about 75% of his customers pay using subsidies he called the foundation of the business. Adam Killa noted demand collapsed after a similar scheme ended in 2022. The article notes heat pumps lag far behind Norway’s installation rate, and that removing funding could threaten apprenticeships and manufacturers, with one economist warning it undermines reindustrialisation efforts. A government spokesperson said it does not comment on budget speculation but remains committed to lowering bills while investing in clean energy. Installers fear the worst as spending is cut.
items.title: UK Heat Pump Installers Warn of Damage from Planned Subsidy Cuts

items.summary: UN special envoy Miguel Angel Moratinos likened the growth of anti-Muslim hatred in Europe to a 'metastasis,' telling Anadolu that hostility had become embedded in political discourse and institutions. He cited rising incidents, including 5,132 hate crimes against Muslims in England and Wales through March 2026 (Home Office) and 4,096 documented cases in Germany in 2025 by CLAIM versus 3,080 the prior year with 214 bodily-injury cases. Moratinos urged stronger laws, education investment and monitoring mechanisms, arguing ignorance drives prejudice. He also questioned post-Sept. 11 security emphasis and defended international law amid Israel barring UN chief Antonio Guterres from entry.
items.title: UN envoy compares Europe's Islamophobia spread to metastasis

items.summary: Tamil Nadu Minister Keerthana responded to social media criticism after pictures of her Tirupati temple visit circulated, showing she wore nearly 10 sovereigns of gold. Critics compared this with the three sovereigns disclosed in her election affidavit. She rejected the scrutiny, saying critics cannot “dim a woman who knows why she started,” and credited Chief Minister Vijay for his support.
items.title: TVK minister Keerthana rebuts trolls over gold jewellery at Tirupati

items.summary: Fifteen German photovoltaic developers, including RWE and Enertrag, have called for raising the ground-mounted solar auction price ceiling from €59/MWh to at least €70/MWh in 2027. The group warns that planned policy changes could undermine project economics. They cite a Prognos study commissioned by BDEW estimating levelized costs could rise up to 30%, reaching €13/MWh to €15/MWh above the current ceiling, and propose a sliding formula from early 2028 with an 8% buffer capped at €70/MWh.
items.title: German Solar Developers Seek Higher 2027 Auction Ceiling

items.summary: Threats Without Borders newsletter Issue 310 surveys recent cybercrime activity and commentary from author Matt. It notes that companies including PWC, J.B. Hunt, AB InBev and Whirlpool appeared on the ransomware time clock in the past week, arguing no network is truly secure because modern organizations have expanded attack surfaces with acquisitions, software and remote workers. The piece references David Bianco's Pyramid of Pain to advocate for behavior-based detection over blocking hashes or IPs. It also covers a Federal Trade Commission report estimating fraud costs to older adults could reach $119.5 billion in 2025; the launch of the Justice Department's Fraud Whistleblower Incentive Program offering rewards from $10,000 to $30,000; arrests tied to a $1.23 million Walmart account fraud scheme; and a Wisconsin school district losing approximately $92,000 in a business email compromise attack. The newsletter closes with reflections on the curse of knowledge.
items.title: Cybersecurity Newsletter Reviews Ransomware, Fraud and Legal Cases

items.summary: Donald Trump called former FBI director James Comey a “dirty cop” after the US justice department filed criminal information to prosecute him for sharing classified national security information with a New York Times reporter in 2016. Comey maintains his innocence, and lawyers are seeking dismissal.
items.title: Trump Calls Comey a Dirty Cop as Third Prosecution Advances

items.summary: New Justice Minister Takashi Yamashita expressed eagerness in an interview to legalize the sole use of maiden names after marriage. He said details remain under consideration and that a selective dual surname system is a separate issue from establishing such a legal basis.
items.title: Justice Minister Yamashita Eager to Legalize Sole Maiden Name Use

items.summary: Federal prosecutors have filed a court document seeking criminal charges against former FBI Director James Comey over an alleged disclosure of classified information to the New York Times in October 2016. This is the third time the justice department has moved to bring criminal charges against Comey, who was a longtime critic of President Donald Trump. Comey's lawyers say the case stems from that 2016 disclosure and deny wrongdoing. His attorney Patrick Fitzgerald filed a motion to dismiss, arguing prosecutors are charging crimes he did not commit. Former prosecutor Glenn Kirschner told the BBC the case may exceed the statute of limitations. Law professor Jessica Levinson noted details remain slim because the charges stay under seal.
items.title: Ex-FBI Director James Comey Faces Third Federal Charging Action

items.summary: The Digital News Publishers Association (DNPA), representing 21 digital news publishers, challenged the Centre’s Digital Personal Data Protection Act before a Supreme Court Bench on Tuesday. Its senior advocate Madhavi Divan argued that enforcing the law without an exemption for journalism would force newsrooms to shut down and impose pre-censorship. The court declined an interim stay without hearing the Union ministries of Law and Justice and Electronics and Information Technology, listing the matter for November 17. Divan said earlier versions excluded journalism, suggesting it was never meant for her clients.
items.title: Digital News Publishers Association Challenges DPDP Law in Supreme Court

items.summary: Government actions and corporate moves highlighted the increasing importance of data centers in national economies and business planning, even as resistance to these large projects grows across much of the West. Spain relaxed renewable power requirements for new sites after industry pushback, while Microsoft excluded related staff from buyouts during cost-cutting, and Anthropic noted in its IPO filing that power access remains a major concern.
items.title: Data Centers Gain Strategic Importance Amid Growing Opposition Across Western Nations and Corporations

items.summary: A new NPR/PBS News/Marist poll indicates that Democrats hold significant advantages heading into the midterm elections and are favored to gain control of the U.S. House, according to a report from Up First. NPR's Domenico Montanaro told the program that Democrats carry an 8-point advantage among likely voters on the generic congressional ballot. While it seems unlikely Democrats will lose the House, the Senate remains a toss-up, with close races expected to remain unclear through vote counting days after election night. The item also covers Israel's high-stakes parliamentary election held amid expectations of strong voter turnout and significant national stakes following last year's Hamas attacks.
items.title: Poll Shows Democrats Hold Midterm Edge as Israel Votes

items.summary: Researchers from Shedd Aquarium, Arkansas State University, and the USGS described five new-to-science freshwater mussel species from rivers across Missouri, Arkansas, Mississippi, Alabama, Louisiana, and Texas, published in Zootaxa. The shells resembled known species, so the team sequenced three genes and compared more than 440 shell outlines after two decades of fieldwork. Several are rare and confined to single basins; only one has been proposed for federal protection. Nathan Johnson noted the findings show how much remains unknown about river biodiversity. Alan Lymbery added that mussels often cannot recover from large death events as keystone species, underscoring their conservation importance.
items.title: Five New Mussel Species Revealed Through DNA in U.S. Rivers

items.summary: Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi announced her upcoming memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, which is scheduled to be released on November 10. She said she wrote the book to recount events as they happened rather than let others define her life and experiences, noting that much written about her had been invented or exaggerated. Anticipating mixed reactions, Gandhi remarked there would be some tamasha when it comes out, acknowledging some readers might change their views while others could become more negative. The memoir traces her journey from childhood in Italy to India as the wife of former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi and daughter-in-law of Indira Gandhi, whose assassination occurred in 1984.
items.title: ‘There’s bound to be some tamasha’: Sonia Gandhi on her upcoming memoir ‘Belonging’

items.summary: The Chief Electoral Officer's office said Karnataka's Special Intensive Revision cut the state's final voter list to 4.54 crore from a pre-revision 5.54 crore, after excluding 1,08,76,625 enumeration forms and marking 61,867 electors ineligible following notices and hearings. The revision, launched on June 30 and concluded on October 22, was the state's first intensive roll update since 2002.
items.title: Karnataka deletes over one crore names in voter roll revision

items.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio confirmed on Monday that the United States told Venezuelan officials “weeks and weeks ago” opposition leader María Corina Machado should be allowed to return, according to EL PAÍS USA Edition. He said the White House only discouraged her return in the days after the June 24 earthquakes, when humanitarian aid was the priority. Machado had tried returning at least seven times since early September.
items.title: Rubio Says U.S. Told Venezuela Weeks Ago Machado Could Return

items.summary: Rising global diesel and gasoline prices lifted India's fuel export value by 50% in rupee terms between April and September, per oil ministry data cited by The Economic Times. Total earnings reached $27.2 billion as regional benchmarks hit record highs after the Iran war disrupted supplies. Diesel alone drove a 58% jump to $12.6 billion despite falling volumes. Oil Minister Hardeep Puri said India would keep exporting diesel to ease global shortages, citing expanding refining capacity toward 6.4 million barrels per day by 2032.
items.title: India's Diesel Exports Lift Fuel Earnings Amid Middle East Crisis

items.summary: The Netherlands has withdrawn from next year's Eurovision Song Contest, reversing a pledge to return in 2027 after public broadcaster NPO cited sensitivities over Israel's participation. NPO chair Jet de Ranitz said the organisation could not find a suitable format and concluded it was too early to take part. The contest will still be aired there; organisers say they welcome a Dutch entry when the time is right.
items.title: Netherlands Withdraws From Eurovision Over Israel Participation

items.summary: Stellantis México submitted an environmental impact assessment to Semarnat for two solar plants totaling 21.56 MWp at its industrial complex in Saltillo, Coahuila. The project will supply electricity to the automaker’s facilities without exporting surplus power and is expected to generate about 51.68 GWh annually. It builds on Stellantis’ partnership with Argentine company 360Energy, which acquired a 49.5% stake in 2024.
items.title: Stellantis Submits Plan for Solar Plants at Saltillo Complex
